title: AI-derived marrow PET measures correlate with myeloma burden
summary: A convolutional network segmented whole-body bones in PET/CT scans from 35 untreated patients with multiple myeloma. Metabolic-volume measures derived using four of six uptake thresholds showed moderate associations with biopsy plasma-cell infiltration and blood beta-2-microglobulin. Results depended on the chosen threshold and remain exploratory; the study did not establish survival prediction, treatment response or replacement of marrow biopsy.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network; automated skeletal segmentation
organization: German Cancer Research Center; Heidelberg University Hospital; Chalmers University of Technology; Eigenvision

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Clinical associations of automated PET measurements with iliac-crest biopsy infiltration and blood beta-2-microglobulin in 35 untreated patients.
evidence.unknown: Threshold generalizability, clinical utility and outcome prediction remain unestablished; individual lesions were generally not biopsied and skull/large lytic lesions can be missed.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN segments bones and reference tissues, enabling volumetric metabolic measurements that are compared with independently measured clinical biomarkers.
